text:
omar: Heads-up — planning a focused benchmark run for long-context / prefill-dominant mixes. Goal: reproduce the ~2.8x tail regression we saw last week and validate the kernel-selection fixes. Running on repro infra. Need alignment on configs + metrics. :wave:

jia: SG. Are we combining replay harness + synthetic long-tail or running them separately?

omar: Plan = three workload shapes:
- PREFILL_ONLY: single large prefill (>=1024 tokens) then short streaming responses (prefill-dominant)
- MIXED_LONGTAIL: a context-mix with ~30% prefill-heavy requests and 70% short requests (seq32)
- REPLAY_BENCH: production replay normalized for request-rate (seeded)

sam: For apples-to-apples we must keep model, quant, and KV-policy identical across baseline/patch runs. Which model/quant are we using?

omar: Use rwd-ggml-7B-fp16 as baseline, rwd-ggml-7B-4bitq as comparator. KV-policy: sticky-prefill, TTL=300s, eviction LRU disabled for these runs to isolate prefill behavior.

maria: We should also log kernel-chooser traces: for every decoding step emit chosen_kernel, seq_len, kv_size, step_time. Tag runs with kernel-chooser:v2 so diffs are easier.

kenneth: Minimal metric set: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU occupancy, kernel-time breakdown (matmul, softmax, kv-lookup), batch-size distribution, and per-request memory usage.

ci-bot: Deploy started: benchmark-run/1893456789 on infra-runner-12 (cmd: ./bench_runner --cfg longmix.yaml) :rocket:

jia: Quick config snippet to put in bench repo:
```
workload:
  name: mixed_longtail
  duration: 30m
  seq_dist: {1024:0.25,512:0.25,256:0.2,64:0.2,32:0.1}
generators:
  - replay_seed: prod-2026-11-01-abc
  - synthetic_ratio: 0.4
kernels:
  chooser_trace: true
  force_kernel: auto
```

sam: Two experiment notes:
1) Run baseline (main@a1b2c) then patch (kernel-pr/789). Keep GPU instance type identical.
2) Temporarily disable the batching heuristic that coalesces across prefill boundaries — we've seen head-of-line blocking there.

maria: Profiling tip: enable sampling profiler @10ms and also collect our microtimers around kv_cache.get and prefill_flush. In the repro I saw ~12% of time spent in prefill_flush before any fixes.

omar: If we observe KV eviction thrash, switch harness to per-request sticky caching and re-run (helps isolate eviction-induced lat spikes).

kenneth: Hypothesis: kernel selector prefers a large-matmul kernel at seq=512 which causes working set blowup when KV cache grows -> latent OOM-like latency spikes. Add guard: prefer streaming kernel when kv_size > 200MB.

jia: Analysis checklist we want after runs:
- apples-to-apples diff: per-step kernel-choice heatmap
- cost-per-token delta and absolute tokens/sec
- latency CDF overlays for all workloads (baseline vs patch)
- top-5 regression spots with kernel id + line numbers / flame samples

sam: I'll run the two 30m jobs back-to-back tonight and post raw trace links when done.

omar: If nondeterministic spikes appear, pin RNGs and increase replay ratio. Also set bench concurrency low to reduce noise. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: Benchmark update: baseline finished (1893456802), patched run queued (1893456829). Artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-bench/1893456789/{baseline,patched}/

maria: Perfect — once patched results are in let's sync 11:00 tomorrow for triage. I'll prep visual diffs and the kernel-choice heatmaps.

omar: Thanks all — appreciate quick turnaround.
